hotContext.criticalNews: Q2 2026 earnings (July 22): record $28.2B revenue and already-known 480k deliveries, but non-GAAP EPS $0.33 (miss), op margin 1.4%, FCF −$1.09B on $5.8B CapEx. Regulatory credits collapsed to $146M. TSLA −~14.5% on July 23. Volume without profit; full-year CapEx >$25B keeps auto P&L under pressure.

recentKeyChanges.title: TSLA -26% in July — worst month since December 2022
recentKeyChanges.description: The Q2 earnings miss (EPS $0.33 vs $0.53 expected, 1.4% op margin, -$1.09B FCF) triggered a month-long selloff from ~$425 to ~$311. Continued analyst note-writing extended the move through late July. Stock is now down ~30% YTD. Market is explicitly repricing Tesla on profit quality failure, not delivery volume. The ~$320 close on July 23 erased >$140B in market cap in a single session, and the bleed continued through month-end.

sentiment.headline: negative
sentiment.rationale: Stock action and analyst coverage uniformly negative post-earnings. No recovery catalyst emerged in the two weeks following the print.

recentKeyChanges.title: Broad analyst price target cuts post-earnings — Hold cluster at $375-400 now institutional consensus
recentKeyChanges.description: No upward PT revisions post-Q2 earnings. Goldman Sachs, Truist, and Morgan Stanley all moved to Hold at ~$375-400. Piper Sandler cut from $500 to $450 on July 28 (stock fell an additional 1.2% that session). Wells Fargo and JPMorgan maintained Underweight at $130-145. Wedbush remained the only notable outlier at $600 Buy. Full-year 2026 EPS consensus cut from ~$1.89 pre-earnings to ~$1.37 post-earnings — a ~28% reduction driven by the operating margin miss and structural loss of regulatory credit revenue.

sentiment.headline: negative
sentiment.rationale: Uniform analyst PT cuts with no upgrades reflects broad institutional consensus that Q2 profit quality was structurally poor, not a one-quarter anomaly.

recentKeyChanges.title: Full-year 2026 delivery consensus revised to ~1.65M — barely 1% growth vs 2025
recentKeyChanges.description: Post-Q2 analyst consensus for full-year 2026 deliveries was cut from ~1.69M to ~1.65M. Q2's 480k beat was inventory-fed (production 28k below deliveries), not a demand re-acceleration. Musk's 20-30% growth guidance — implying ~1.9-2.0M deliveries — is now widely viewed as unreachable by Street consensus. Q3 2026 IR delivery consensus had not yet been published as of August 6. The ~1.65M full-year estimate implies H2 run-rate roughly flat with H1, with no major model refresh or new market entry expected to accelerate volume.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Headlines emphasize Q2 delivery beat; underlying reality is full-year consensus implies ~1% YoY growth vs management's 20-30% target — a massive guidance miss in the making.
